title: When you need to return to Hukam
issueStatement: The mind is pushing hard against reality, trying to secure itself through control, explanation, or resistance.
centralInsight: Hukam is not fatalism. It is the truthful frame within which the self becomes quieter and more teachable.
practicalReflection: Hukam does not erase action. It purifies the spirit in which action happens.
actionPrompt: Name where you are acting faithfully and where you are merely fighting what already is.

repair.label: After the Slip
repair.title: Hukam after the slip
repair.issueStatement: The mind wants reality to arrive on self-approved terms. The wound or failure has already happened, and the next task is to return truthfully instead of rehearsing despair.
repair.centralInsight: Guru reframes peace as understanding the command already holding everything. Gurbani keeps repair close to humility, remembrance, and return instead of theatre.
repair.practicalReflection: Repair becomes honest when the mind stops turning failure into identity and lets the next true act matter.
repair.actionPrompt: Name one thing already here that you need to stop negotiating with. Choose the next truthful return instead of rehearsing the failure.

practice.label: Steady Practice
practice.title: Building a truer practice of hukam
practice.issueStatement: The mind wants reality to arrive on self-approved terms. The deeper need is a form of return that can outlast novelty, urgency, and mood.
practice.centralInsight: Guru reframes peace as understanding the command already holding everything. The teaching becomes durable when it is practiced repeatedly enough to change posture.
practice.practicalReflection: Practice matters because the heart is always being trained by something; Gurbani asks what pattern is becoming ordinary.
practice.actionPrompt: Name one thing already here that you need to stop negotiating with. Repeat what you can actually keep.
